objectives: To provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the historical development, philosophical foundations, and legal frameworks of human rights at both national and international levels.
To explore key international human rights instruments such as treaties, conventions, and organizations, including the role of the United Nations, in promoting and protecting human rights.

To examine the intersection of human rights and international affairs, focusing on how global political issues like international conflicts, foreign policy, and development impact the human rights agenda.
To critically analyze contemporary human rights challenges and case studies from an interdisciplinary perspective, encompassing political, legal, and ethical dimensions.
To assess the role of state and non-state actors in the implementation and violation of human rights, and explore the impact of international interventions, sanctions, and humanitarian efforts.
To encourage students to engage in human rights advocacy and policy analysis, focusing on the formulation of policies and interventions to address human rights violations in global contexts.
course_outcomes: Develop a strong foundation in human rights frameworks, understanding their historical, legal, and philosophical aspects at national and international levels.
Critically assess the role of international human rights instruments and organizations, and their impact on global issues.
Analyze the intersection of human rights and international affairs, exploring the influence of global politics, conflicts, and policies on human rights.
Foster skills in human rights advocacy and policy-making, enabling students to address violations and contribute to global solutions. Pre-requisite of course:None

COURSE CODE     10PS0804
COURSE CREDITS  4

Objective:
 1  To provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the historical development,
     philosophical foundations, and legal frameworks of human rights at both national and
     international levels.
 2  To explore key international human rights instruments such as treaties, conventions, and
     organizations, including the role of the United Nations, in promoting and protecting human
      rights.
 3  To examine the intersection of human rights and international affairs, focusing on how
     global political issues like international conflicts, foreign policy, and development impact
     the human rights agenda.
 4  To critically analyze contemporary human rights challenges and case studies from an
     interdisciplinary perspective, encompassing political, legal, and ethical dimensions.
 5  To assess the role of state and non-state actors in the implementation and violation of
    human rights, and explore the impact of international interventions, sanctions, and
     humanitarian efforts.
 6  To encourage students to engage in human rights advocacy and policy analysis, focusing
    on the formulation of policies and interventions to address human rights violations in
     global contexts.


Course Outcomes: After completion of this course, student will be able to:
 1  Develop a strong foundation in human rights frameworks, understanding their historical,
      legal, and philosophical aspects at national and international levels.
 2   Critically assess the role of international human rights instruments and organizations, and
      their impact on global issues.
 3  Analyze the intersection of human rights and international affairs, exploring the influence
     of global politics, conflicts, and policies on human rights.
 4  Foster skills in human rights advocacy and policy-making, enabling students to address
     violations and contribute to global solutions.
